passage_text: Researchers studied the effect of a novel dietary supplement on the recovery time of athletes after a 10‑km run. Twenty‑eight male participants were randomly assigned to either the supplement group (n=14) or a placebo group (n=14). All participants performed a standardized 10‑km time trial, received their assigned intervention immediately after completion, and then recorded their recovery time (time until heart rate returned to 70% of resting value). The table below summarizes the mean recovery times (in minutes) and the standard deviations for each group. The study aimed to determine whether the supplement significantly reduced recovery time compared to placebo.
table_data:
Group | Mean Recovery Time (min) | Standard Deviation
--- | --- | ---
Supplement | 12.4 | 1.8
Placebo | 14.7 | 2.1
stem: Based on the data presented, which statement accurately reflects the study’s findings?

options.A: The supplement group had a faster mean recovery time than the placebo group.
options.B: The placebo group had a faster mean recovery time than the supplement group.
options.C: Both groups had identical mean recovery times.
options.D: The data are insufficient to determine any difference.

explanation: The mean recovery time for the supplement group is 12.4 minutes, which is shorter than the placebo group’s 14.7 minutes, indicating a faster recovery.
trap: Option B incorrectly reverses the direction of the difference.

stem: Which design feature stated in the passage best supports a causal conclusion about the supplement?

options.A: Random assignment of participants to supplement or placebo
options.C: Use of a standardized 10‑km time trial

explanation: Correct: A) Random assignment balances known and unknown differences between groups, so a difference in recovery can be attributed to the supplement. Why the others are wrong: B) Restricting to males narrows the population but does not balance groups. C) Standardizing the run reduces variability but does not balance participant differences. D) Recording the outcome measures it but does not support causation.
trap: Choosing the standardized time trial because it sounds rigorous; it reduces variability in the workload but only random assignment balances the groups.

stem: What is the relative reduction in mean recovery time in the supplement group compared to placebo?
explanation: Correct: A) (14.7 - 12.4)/14.7 = 0.157, about 0.16. Why the others are wrong: B) 0.19 divides the 2.3 min difference by the supplement mean (12.4) instead of the placebo reference. C) 0.33 does not follow from the data. D) 0.45 does not follow from the data.
trap: Dividing the 2.3 min difference by the supplement mean of 12.4 (0.19) instead of by the placebo mean of 14.7.

stem: Which of the following statements is NOT supported by the passage and table?

options.A: Mean recovery time was 2.3 minutes shorter with the supplement.
options.B: Recovery times were more variable in the placebo group (SD 2.1) than in the supplement group (SD 1.8).
options.D: The supplement is effective for all athletic populations.

explanation: Correct: D) Only 28 male participants completed one 10-km trial, so effectiveness in all athletic populations is not supported. Why the others are wrong: A) 14.7 - 12.4 = 2.3 min. B) SDs are 2.1 and 1.8. C) The passage states n = 14 per group.
trap: Generalizing a result in 28 male runners to all athletes because the difference looks large; the data cover only the studied group.

stem: Which physiological process most directly governs how quickly heart rate falls after exercise ends?

options.A: Parasympathetic (vagal) reactivation together with withdrawal of sympathetic drive
options.B: Rising sympathetic drive that keeps heart rate elevated
options.C: The maximal oxygen uptake reached during the run
options.D: A permanent decrease in resting stroke volume

explanation: Correct: A) After exercise, vagal tone returns and sympathetic activity falls, which lowers heart rate. Why the others are wrong: B) Rising sympathetic drive would slow recovery. C) VO2 max describes aerobic capacity, not the rate of heart-rate decline. D) Resting stroke volume is not a post-exercise recovery mechanism and need not change.
trap: Choosing VO2 max because it is the best-known fitness measure; it describes aerobic capacity, whereas recovery speed reflects autonomic reactivation.
